text:
nate: Quick idea — add a ‘backpressure grace window’ to the automatic fallback UX so we don't flip flop when a noisy spike clears quickly. Thoughts? :thinking:
anya: Yes please. We've seen oscillation when a node pool recovers and then falls again. A time-based buffer would help. :+1:
kevin: Agree but want to avoid masking real failures. Maybe combine time window with a minimum sustained error ratio?
rebecca: fwiw ops prefers sample-based thresholds over fixed time. e.g., require X consecutive failing samples before trigger. Less brittle across different traffic patterns.
sam-platform: What about making it configurable in the rollout policy UI: two knobs — grace_window_ms and recovery_sample_count. Default conservative values, advanced mode for power users.
anya: UI question: do we show the live countdown/active grace state in the operator inbox? Operators need to know why an endpoint didn't immediately fallback. :eyes:
ops-bot: [incident] 4290001109 - autoswitch attempted but held by grace window (policy id: p-91). More details at https://console.redwood.internal/policies/p-91 :information_source:
kevin: For auditability we should log both the trigger event and the decision to defer because of grace. So later playback shows the why. Add an event type like AUTOSWITCH_DEFERRED with metadata.
rebecca: Also surface a metric: fallback_defer_duration and fallback_defer_count so SRE can tune.
nate: Prototype config block for discussion:
```
autoswitch:
  enabled: true
  grace_window_ms: 30000   # time to wait after first error spike
  recovery_sample_count: 5 # number of consecutive healthy samples to resume
  error_ratio_threshold: 0.5 # fraction of recent requests classified as errors
```
kevin: Suggest change: sample_count window should be sliding and weighted by recency. Otherwise bursty recovery looks the same as steady recovery.
anya: UX: in rollout timeline show soft-state (orange) while grace window is active, green when resumed, red when fallback engaged. Hover explains reason + link to audit events.
sam-platform: One more: operator override button should allow immediate force-fallback or force-recover with reason. Those overrides must be recorded and visible in audits.
rebecca: Cost note: longer grace windows can increase tail latency / cost if the platform keeps trying the expensive model. We should default to short windows for hosted usage, longer for dedicated/private where recovery costs are different.
nate: Good point, maybe policy templates per deployment tier: hosted/default 10s, dedicated 30s, private 60s.
kevin: API shape for policy update (for SDK):
```
PATCH /v1/policies/{id}
{ "autoswitch": { "grace_window_ms": 30000, "recovery_sample_count": 5 } }
```
rebecca: We should add server-side validation to prevent grace_window_ms > 5m unless account-level flag.
anya: Quick UX follow-up: add a small tooltip copy — "Grace window: temporary buffer to avoid oscillation; changes will be logged for audit." Simple.
sam-platform: +1. I'll draft a console mock and a telemetry schema for AUTOSWITCH_DEFERRED with fields: policy_id, reason, start_ts, end_ts, deferred_by (system/operator).
nate: Who wants to own a short spike simulation to validate defaults? I can run a canary job if @kevin or @sam-platform can wire the test harness.
kevin: I can wire it. I'll push a small harness that toggles error ratio and records decisions.
rebecca: Let's also add an eval: run 1000 simulated requests with spike patterns and measure oscillation count with and without grace window.
anya: Sounds good. Thanks all — I'll add this to the rollout UX spec doc and mockups. :thumbsup:
__note: All fields are strings or list of strings per agents.md. Thread is a continuous single string of messages with sender prefixes.
